description: If you have ADHD, task paralysis is real — your brain needs urgency or novelty to fire the start signal, which is why 'I'll do it in five minutes' becomes four days. This short explains the interest-based nervous system and why timing is everything for ADHD task initiation. Follow for daily ADHD content.

title: Time Blindness: Your Brain Only Has Now and Not-Now #Shorts
description: If the future feels like it does not exist until it is already happening, that is time blindness — one of the most common and least talked-about ADHD patterns. It is not laziness or bad planning. It is a real neurological difference in how the ADHD brain perceives the passage of time. Follow for daily ADHD content.

voiceover: You pushed through for weeks. Every task, every deadline, every 'I'm fine.' Then one Tuesday you cannot get out of bed and you call yourself lazy. That's not laziness. That's ADHD burnout. Here's the cycle: your brain runs on dopamine, and it already starts low. When you hyperfocus or mask or white-knuckle through a hard week, you burn through that dopamine reserve faster than it refills. Eventually the tank hits zero. Executive function drops out completely. You can't start, can't decide, can't feel anything. That crash isn't weakness, it's a withdrawal. To break the cycle you have to refill before empty. Pick one thing daily that gives your brain dopamine without cost: ten minutes outside, one song you love, movement you don't hate. Not a reward for finishing. A refill on a schedule. Follow for daily ADHD content.
